args.text: When naming BPMN events and activities, use concise labels that faithfully preserve the actions, actors, and meaning stated in the process description; avoid adding, omitting, or changing semantic details.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already addresses faithful BPMN labeling.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.

args.text: When naming BPMN events and activities, use concise labels that faithfully preserve the actions, actors, and meaning stated in the process description; avoid adding, omitting, or changing semantic details.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers faithful, concise element labels.

result.rule: When the description names an activity or outcome with multiple stated actions, alternatives, or a distinguishing object or participant.: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or event so its described scope remains identifiable. Preserve materially stated actions, alternatives, and objects or participants; do not substitute a broader or different action or add unsupported details.

When the description gives contextual details or examples alongside a single activity, without presenting them as separate actions: label the BPMN task with its core action and object; omit contextual details and qualifiers that are not needed to identify the activity

When the description distinguishes different actions or process states involving the same participant or subject at different stages: Label each BPMN activity and outcome to reflect the specific action or state described at that stage; do not substitute a different action or an unsupported outcome.

When the description states a core activity and separately describes a condition or later outcome that marks its completion: Label the BPMN activity with its core action and object; do not add the separately stated completion condition or later outcome to the activity label.
